subject: Next steps: Private VPC qualification — cert provisioning, egress IPs, proxy model
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwoodinference.com>
To: Charlie Ortiz <charlie.ortiz@finexcap.com>, netops@finexcap.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 05 May 2027 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Private VPC qualification — quick recap & ask

Hi Charlie / Finex team — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and concrete asks so we can size the Private VPC work and map next steps: 

- Deployment intent: Finex wants full isolation for PII workloads and plans to run inference against customer data in a dedicated Private VPC. You indicated PrivateLink is preferred but we should confirm compatibility with your ingress/egress policies.
- Outstanding network questions we need from you:
  1) Will you accept a PrivateLink (AWS) endpoint, or do you require VPC peering?
  2) Do you have a central egress NAT or firewall that needs a fixed outbound IP range? If so please provide the allowlist range or the policy owner.
  3) Certificate model: will you provide SAN TLS certificates for the PrivateLink endpoint, or should Redwood provision and rotate certs via your CA?

Attachments: I included a short deployment-ops-matrix to show how each mode (Hosted / Dedicated / Private VPC) maps to network and security expectations — please review.

Next steps I propose:
- Charlie: confirm PrivateLink vs peering preference and provide firewall contact + any existing allowlist ranges (we need IPs if you expect fixed egress).
- Finex procure: we’ll share a simple SOW and pointer to the SOC2 evidence pack once the network model is agreed.
- Marissa/Jordan: can you confirm if we have constraints on cert types or a preferred rotation cadence for PrivateLink endpoints?

Target: capture answers in the sheet and schedule a short handoff call with NetOps (30 min) next week.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
aditya@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0194
Redwood Inference — Production-first LLM inference

Attachment: deployment-ops-matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet, 43 KB)

From: Charlie Ortiz <charlie.ortiz@finexcap.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: netops@finexcap.com, procure@finexcap.com
Date: Wed, 05 May 2027 17:24:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Private VPC qualification — quick recap & ask

Thanks Aditya — good write-up. A few answers from our side: 

1) PrivateLink is our preference (we run multiple SaaS connectors that way). Peering would be our fallback if there are feature gaps.
2) Egress: our security team requires that Redwood provide a small set of static egress IP(s) for allowlisting on our firewall. I don’t have the ranges yet — looping NetOps (netops@finexcap.com) to provide.
3) Certs: we prefer that vendors support customer-supplied certs; our PKI team will issue a SAN cert for the endpoint and handle rotation. If Redwood has an integration pattern for cert deployment/automation (ACME or API-based upload), that would be ideal.

NetOps note (from netops@finexcap.com): we’ll provide firewall owner and existing allowlist ranges by EOD Friday. Also clarify whether Redwood’s egress is a single static IP or a small CIDR (we prefer a single IP).

Procurement: sending a heads-up — we’ll likely request the standard SOW + responsibility matrix.

Charlie Ortiz
Infrastructure Operations Manager | Finex Capital
charlie.ortiz@finexcap.com

Subject: Re: Post-call: Private VPC qualification — quick recap & ask

Appreciate the quick turn, Charlie. A few clarifications from our side so NetOps has what they need: 

- Egress IPs: Redwood can publish a small set of static egress addresses per-customer when running in Private VPC mode behind our egress NAT. Typical pattern is 1–4 addresses (single IP preferred for firewall simplicity). We can allocate dedicated egress IP(s) for Finex.
- Certs: we support two flows: (A) Customer-supplied SAN cert (uploaded to our control plane) with automated rotation hooks; (B) Redwood-managed certs where we act as the cert operator and push certs to the endpoint (we provide rotation logs). If Finex wants PKI-managed rotation, flow A is best.
- Proxy / outbound inspection: If your firewall inspects TLS upstream, we can terminate TLS at the PrivateLink endpoint using the customer cert; traffic from Redwood into backend services will then use our internal mTLS for inter-service calls.

Attached is a condensed Private VPC checklist showing the exact items we need from NetOps to complete qualification (egress addr, allowed ports, cert CN/SAN list). If NetOps can fill the checklist and drop it back we will schedule a 30-min handoff with our network engineers.

Next action owners:
- NetOps (Finex): provide allowlist IP(s) or CIDR, owner contact, and confirm any deep-packet-inspection rules that would require cert termination.
- Marissa (Redwood): prepare SOW template and the SOC2 evidence pointer for procurement.
- Jordan (Redwood): prepare short runbook for cert upload steps and a staging timeline (we recommend a 2-week staging window).

Thanks — happy to jump on a NetOps call once we have the allowlist.

Aditya Rao
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Attachment: private-vpc-checklist.pdf (PDF, 26 KB)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Thu, 06 May 2027 09:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Private VPC qualification — quick recap & ask

Thanks — quick technical notes from our infra team: 

- Egress model: we can allocate a single static public IP for Finex’s outbound traffic from the Redwood side. This IP will be announced from our egress NAT in the region you select (US-West). If you require multiple IPs for HA, we can provide a /29 on request but that adds a bit more coordination.
- TLS certs: customer-supplied SAN certs must include the endpoint FQDN we create (e.g., vpce-finex-prod.redwood-inference.com). We support PKCS#12 and PEM bundles via our control plane API; rotation can be automated using a webhook to your PKI team (we will call back to trigger uploads if you prefer).
- DPI / proxy: if your firewall performs TLS inspection, we recommend customer cert termination at the PrivateLink to avoid downstream breakage. If you need us to support proxy passthrough, call that out and we’ll share a short compatibility note (there are edge cases with ALPN and gRPC streaming).

Staging suggestion:
1) NetOps provides a one-line confirmation of allowed egress IP (or target to allowlist).
2) We provision a staging PrivateLink endpoint and share DNS + cert CN to Finex PKI.
3) Finex uploads cert (or authorizes Redwood-managed cert).
4) Smoke test with limited traffic (we’ll provide a test harness).

I’ll block 30 minutes Friday 11:00 AM PT for a NetOps handoff — if that works for your team please reply with attendees.

Jordan Blake
Principal Cloud Architect | Redwood Inference
jordan_blake@redwoodinference.com
